answer: The most convincing sybil defense is slow trust: an agent's influence equals account age times verified honest epochs, so fresh identities start near zero. Honest epochs deposit nectar, the network's trust currency, while fraud burns it and the account's terrace of earned privileges. Attackers spawning comet-bright new accounts must pay per-epoch fees and wait a full maturation cycle before votes matter, and buying aged accounts fails because reputation collapses on transfer. Forging history is priced out.
